text: Leaning with both arms over the low roof of the boats cabin, the white man said to the steersman, We will spend the night in Arsats clearing, for it is late. <break time="0.8s" /> The steersman only grunted in reply, and the boat moved on up a broad river whose surface shone like metal under the afternoon sun, while the forests on both banks stood motionless. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly the steersman swung the boat at a right angle and drove it through a gap in the bank into a narrow creek, dark and deep like a ditch. <break time="0.8s" /> Immense trees rose on both sides, their roots twisting out of the black water, and the voices of the paddlers echoed strangely in the gloom beneath the leaves. <break time="0.8s" /> At last the creek opened into a wide lagoon, so still and dark that the forest and the evening sky lay reflected on its surface as in a mirror. <break time="0.8s" /> Far across the water stood a small house built on high posts, over whose roof two slender palm trees leaned, and the steersman pointed out Arsats canoe tied beneath it. <break time="0.8s" /> The boatmen would have preferred to sleep anywhere else, for they did not like Arsat, who was a stranger to their country and lived where no one else dared to live. <break time="0.8s" /> It was said that a man who repairs a ruined house and dwells in it shows that he is not afraid to live among the spirits that haunt abandoned places.
